correctness.rationale: Janson's Jefferson seat-excess limit gives the on-slice modal displacement law; boundedness upgrades weak convergence to all polynomial moments. Bernoulli-polynomial generating functions then give the all-order universal c_k means, and an independent conditional-uniform calculation yields the Q2 formula. A deterministic low-order enumeration agrees numerically.

originality.rationale: The recent multinomial-mode paper explicitly leaves modal on-slice Cesaro averaging open, while Janson supplies the older seat-excess limit law. Targeted searches did not locate the all-order universal logarithmic coefficient formula, the explicit Q2 heterogeneity term, or the normalized modal-mass consequence. Older apportionment moment literature remains a residual risk, so the claim is only to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result resolves a stated on-slice averaging gap under the generic arithmetic condition, gives a closed all-order law rather than a single correction term, and pinpoints the first order at which the actual probability expansion ceases to be universal.
